subject: Proposal: flexible ramp + multi-year renewal structure
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara.patel@coralytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Li <tom.li@coralytics.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal timing + capacity ramp question

Jordan — thanks for running the renewal number by us during last week’s QBR. Two follow-ups from our side: 1) We’re evaluating whether to move to a 3-year committed schedule with a staged ramp (25% / 35% / 40%) to get better unit pricing, and 2) we want the renewal to co-term with our other infra contracts (September 1).

Can your team lay out the tradeoffs on unit price vs. ramp aggressiveness and whether you can accommodate a co-term amendment mid-year? Also, legal is asking about an auto-renew clause — they prefer an opt-out notice window rather than automatic renewal without notice.

Attaching our internal budget calendar.

— Sara
Director of AI Platform
Coralytics

Attachments: coralytics_budget_q2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara.patel@coralytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + capacity ramp question

Sara — great to hear from you. Short answer: yes, we can do a multi-year commit with a staged ramp and co-term into September, and we can propose an opt-out notice window for auto-renew. I’ve put together a short proposal showing three pricing scenarios (Aggressive ramp / Balanced / Conservative) and a co-term amendment that slides effective date to 2027-09-01. See the attached PDF and spreadsheet for line items and unit deltas.

Key tradeoffs in plain terms:
- Aggressive ramp (front-loaded capacity): lowest blended $/token in year one but higher near-term spend — good if you have immediate product launches.
- Balanced ramp: modest step-down each year; preserves runway and predictable ops.
- Conservative ramp (back-loaded): less cash up-front, slightly higher blended unit price over 3 years.

On renewal mechanics, Marissa will lead commercial, and Karthik can comment on legal language for the opt-out window — recommending 60 days. If that works, I’ll draft the amendment and route it for signatures.

Next step: quick 20-min sync tomorrow to align on scenario preference?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0134

Attachments: Coralytics_Renewal_Proposal_Q2.pdf, Co-term_Schedule.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 08:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + capacity ramp question

Looping in a couple of commercial notes — Jordan, saw your scenarios and added suggested discount tiers tied to committed GPU-hours and cache retention profiles. A couple quick asks for the proposal:
- Add a fallback model variant clause (in case a pinned model is deprecated mid-term) to protect performance SLAs.
- Confirm whether the co-term amendment can be executed as an addendum (no new SOW) so procurement at Coralytics treats it as an amendment rather than a full procurement event.

Karthik — can you draft the opt-out language (60 days) and a 30-day grace period for migration if they downsize commitments? Legal prefers a short grace period to avoid capacity stranded assets.

— Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2027 09:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + capacity ramp question

Marissa / Jordan — draft language below that I recommend for the amendment (high-level summary to include in the proposal):

"Auto-Renew & Opt-Out: Contract will automatically renew for successive one-year terms unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days prior to the then-current term end date. In the event Customer reduces committed capacity at renewal, Customer shall have a 30-day migration window during which Redwood will provide reasonable support to migrate workloads; credits for unused committed capacity may be applied per the schedule in Appendix A."

I also added a short clause for model variant fallback and an explicit definition of "committed capacity" to avoid ambiguity. I’ll prepare a redline version of the amendment doc and attach it to the HubSpot record.

— Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Li <tom.li@coralytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@coralytics.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2027 13:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal timing + capacity ramp question

Jordan / team — thanks for the fast turnaround. Coralytics prefers the Balanced ramp scenario (25% / 35% / 40%), and the ability to co-term to Sept 1 is important for our internal vendor alignment. The 60-day opt-out window sounds reasonable; legal will want the 30-day migration support spelled out in the amendment.

One additional ask: can we include an annual true-up clause rather than a quarterly true-up? Quarterly is operationally noisy for us; annual true-up that reconciles committed GPU-hours vs. consumption is preferable.

If you can update the proposal to reflect annual true-up and the opt-out + migration language, we can get commercial review started and aim for signatures in March.

— Tom
Head of Platform Engineering
Coralytics

Attachment referenced: Coralytics_internal_requirements.pdf (not included)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Team — thanks, all. I updated the proposal PDF and the co-term schedule to reflect: Balanced ramp (25/35/40), annual true-up, 60-day opt-out, and 30-day migration support. Attached is the revised proposal plus a simple amendment doc for legal to review (Proposed_Term_Amendment.docx).

If Coralytics approves these items, next steps: 1) I'll send the amendment for signature via DocuSign, 2) Marissa will prepare the billing schedule and discount tier commitments, and 3) Karthik will attach the redline to the HubSpot deal. Can we lock a signature target of March 18? That gives procurement time to route before the Sept co-term.

Please reply with any final changes — otherwise I’ll kick off the DocuSign flow tomorrow.

Best,
Jordan Blake
